standard_prerequisites.name: The statement that a quasi-compact space has a closed point whose complement is controlled by the standing hypotheses
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 3583-3585)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a point closed in the relevant closed subset.

core_obligations: Translate non-Jacobsonness: there is a closed subset and an open subset meeting it in a nonempty set containing no point closed in the whole space (proof lines 3577-3580)
Shrink the open subset: the basis of quasi-compact opens allows replacing it by a quasi-compact open neighbourhood of a point of that intersection (proof lines 3581-3582)
Produce the point: the closed point statement gives a point closed inside the intersection, which is therefore locally closed but not closed in the space (proof lines 3583-3585)
proof_roadmap: X 非 Jacobson ⇒ 存在闭集 Z 与开集 U 使 Z ∩ U 非空且不含 X 中的闭点。
由准紧开基，可把 U 换成 Z ∩ U 中某点的准紧开邻域 ⇒ 不妨设 U 准紧开。
由「准紧空间的闭点」引理得 x ∈ Z ∩ U 在 Z ∩ U 中闭 ⇒ {x} 局部闭但不在 X 中闭。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a Kolmogorov space with a basis of quasi-compact opens which is not Jacobson possesses a non-closed point whose singleton is locally closed (author lemma at source lines 3569-3575, label lemma-non-jacobson-Noetherian-characterize). The proof (source lines 3577-3586) translates non-Jacobsonness into the existence of a closed set and an open set meeting it without closed points, shrinks the open set using the basis and applies the closed point statement inside the intersection (proof lines 3577-3585). The translation and the shrink are the content. H3.
